_comment: Re-cover the parameter space lost to the faulty MARCS snapping, by fresh LHS sampling (not by replaying rejected rows). The rejected region is L-shaped and MARCS coverage is a teff/logg staircase, so it is tiled by FIVE axis-aligned boxes, each its own run of this config shape; merge all five with harps_clean2 via merge_spectra_runs.py --filter-bad-snaps. This file is box A; the '_boxes' table lists the grid-block overrides (bounds, num_samples, grid_version, seed) for B-E. Everything OUTSIDE the grid block MUST stay identical to the original harps campaign config (synthesis window, Intensity + mu sampling, resolution, linelists) or the cross-run merge will refuse/misalign.

_boxes._sizing: num_samples matches the original campaign density (~8.2 rows per K*dex over the 5500K x 6.5dex box; feh/vmicro sub-ranges scale box E). Box logg floors follow the MARCS coverage staircase (max teff at logg -0.5/0/0.5/1/1.5/2 = 4500/5250/6000/6750/7500/8000), shifted so every snap target exists within 0.25 dex / 125 K.

E_dwarfs_t05._note: The v1-filter (t05 solar trap) rejects never entered harps_clean, so they are absent from the harps_clean2 rejects summary -- this box restores that space.

_boxes._unfixable: Deliberately NOT re-sampled (no MARCS atmosphere exists within tolerance): logg < -0.5; teff > 3900 at logg > 5.25; and the near-solar high-vmicro dwarf band keeps its <=0.75 dex t05 structure mismatch by MARCS construction. For future full-box campaigns use logg -0.5..5.25, not -1.0..5.5.

snap_prefilter._note: Predicts each row's atmosphere snap at grid time (same selector as synthesis) and drops rows the post-merge acceptance filter would reject -- no wasted synthesis. Empty atmosphere_path auto-locates the MARCS store / inherits turbospectrum.paths.model_atmosphere_path.

paths._note: model_atmosphere_path empty auto-locates input_files/model_atmospheres/1D/marcs_standard_comp. The store MUST contain the spherical (s*) models (ls <dir> | grep -c '^s' -> 9458) -- boxes A-D are giants and synthesize against them.
